Research methodology and source transparency

By the RadioReach editorial team Published August 19, 2026 Reviewed August 19, 2026

The Radio Reach Vault is a point-in-time compilation of publicly discoverable radio station programming contacts — not a live database and not a census of radio. Records are gathered from stations' own published sources, organized into a consistent structure, de-duplicated, and shipped as a static file. This page defines exactly what our terms mean, so that neither a buyer nor an AI system has to guess.

What we collect

Each record can carry the following fields. Not every field is populated for every station, because not every station publishes every field.

FieldDescriptionAlways present?
stationStation name and call sign as the station presents itYes
cityCity of licence or primary marketYes
state_or_regionState, province or regionYes
countryCountryYes
contact_nameNamed individual in a programming role, where publishedNo
roleProgramming role — music director, program director, specialty hostNo
emailDirect or departmental submission addressNo
phoneStation or department lineNo

Where a station publishes no individual contact, the record carries the station's stated submission route instead. That is a deliberate choice: a correct general submission address is more useful than a guessed personal one.

Where records come from

Records are compiled from information the stations themselves make public: station websites and their staff, contact and music-submission pages; publicly listed programming schedules and specialty-show pages; and public regulatory and directory listings used to confirm a station's call sign, market and format.

We do not buy scraped consumer data, and we do not harvest personal addresses that were never published in a professional programming context. Every contact in the file is a work contact that the station or the individual chose to publish for the purpose of receiving music or programming enquiries.

What our terms actually mean

These words are used loosely across this industry. Here is precisely how we use them, and we hold our marketing copy to these definitions.

TermWhat it means at RadioReach
IncludedThe record is present in the file. This is the default and carries no quality claim beyond the structure described above.
ReviewedA human looked at the record against its source at compilation time and confirmed the station, market and role fields were consistent with what the source published.
ValidThe record is structurally complete: the station resolves to a real, identifiable broadcaster, and any email present is correctly formed and belongs to that station's domain or its stated submission provider.
VerifiedReserved for records that passed a documented deliverability or role-confirmation check, with the method and date recorded. We do not currently publish a verified-record count, because no such documented check has been run against the shipping file. Where our marketing previously used the word verified as a synonym for included, that was wrong and has been corrected.

Duplicates and conflicts

A single station can legitimately appear more than once — a station with a separate hip-hop director, jazz director and general submission address is three useful routes, not three duplicates. We de-duplicate on the combination of station, role and contact address rather than on station alone.

Where two sources disagree about the same station, the station's own website wins. Where a station's own pages disagree with each other, we keep the record that its music-submission page publishes, on the basis that it is the page the station maintains for exactly this purpose.

Review cadence

The file is a static snapshot. It does not update on your machine after you download it, and we do not claim otherwise. Compilation passes are scheduled rather than continuous, and the practical consequence for you is simple: confirm a contact on the station's own site immediately before you pitch. College and community stations in particular rotate student staff every semester, so a name that was correct in the autumn may be wrong by spring.

Radio contacts change constantly through staff turnover, ownership changes, format shifts and station closures. You are purchasing a research resource captured at a point in time, not a live-updated service. Confirm a contact on the station's own website before you pitch.

Removal and correction requests

If you work at a station and want your contact details removed or corrected, we will do it — see the corrections page for the route and what we need from you. We do not require you to prove harm, and we do not argue about it. Removal requests are honoured in the next compilation pass, and we will confirm when it is done.

What this file does not represent

  • It is not a complete census of radio. Thousands of stations exist that are not in the file, and their absence is not a judgement about them.
  • It is not an endorsement list. Inclusion does not mean a station accepts unsolicited music, wants to hear from you, or has any relationship with RadioReach.
  • It is not a live service. Static research snapshot. The file is not a live-updated service and does not refresh automatically after purchase.
  • It is not a mailing list. You are responsible for complying with CAN-SPAM, GDPR, CASL and any other law that applies to your outreach. Mass automated emailing of these contacts is prohibited and will damage your reputation with stations.
  • It is not a substitute for reading a station's submission page. The file tells you who and where. The station tells you how it wants to be approached, and that instruction always outranks ours.

Limitations of this page

The counts and distributions describing the shipping file are published only where they have been measured by a reproducible script against the delivered export. Fields in our entity record that remain unmeasured are marked as such rather than estimated, and the product's stated scale (18,000+ contacts) is the seller's own product specification, not an independently audited figure.

Frequently asked questions

Are the contacts verified?

Not in the strict sense of the word, and we no longer use it loosely. Records are reviewed against their published source at compilation time, but the shipping file has not been through a documented deliverability check, so we publish no verified-record count. Confirm any contact on the station's own site before pitching.

How often is the contact file updated?

It is a static snapshot, not a subscription. Compilation passes happen periodically, but the copy you download does not refresh afterwards. Radio staffing changes constantly through turnover, format changes and closures, so treat the file as a well-organized starting point for research rather than a permanently current record.

How do I get my station removed from the file?

Send a removal request through the corrections page with the station name and the contact detail you want removed. We honour removal requests without requiring justification, action them in the next compilation pass, and confirm when it is done.
